title: The Infinite Labyrinth
subtitle: ENDLESS GENERATION · HOOK TRAJECTORY · TELEPORTATION
description: Explore a fresh, more intricate maze for every ring. Aim with the mouse and throw the chain hook in an arc over the walls. When its path reaches a ring, the ring is consumed and the fire teleports to the ring's floor position as the next maze forms around it.
explanation: The maze is a grid of walkable cells and walls. An iterative depth-first search carves a connected route through every cell; later rooms add extra openings to create alternate paths. A breadth-first search measures reachable distances and chooses a ring tile within hook range. Keyboard movement checks the fire's footprint against the walkable grid. Mouse aiming converts the cursor into a camera ray and intersects it with the ring-height plane. The hook follows a parabolic trajectory whose high point clears the walls, then tests each frame's movement segment against the ring. On a catch, the code saves the ring's floor position, moves the fire there, increments the counter, and generates a new seeded maze around that same position. New rooms keep appearing without a finish screen; their grid grows from 15 × 15 to at most 27 × 27 cells of rendered tiles.
algorithm: DFS carves a connected grid → extra passages add choices → BFS selects a reachable target → mouse ray aims → arcing hook tests each movement segment → catch saves ring position and teleports fire → next seeded maze grows around it
learning_goals: Trace how iterative depth-first search creates connected passages and how added openings change a perfect maze into a maze with loops.
Explain how breadth-first search measures shortest path distance and how the target selector uses that distance.
Follow a mouse position from the screen through a camera ray to a point on a 3D plane.
Describe how a parabolic path clears walls and how segment collision detects a ring between frames.
Trace how the caught ring's saved position becomes the fire's new position and the next maze's origin.
review_points: Why does the depth-first search use a stack, and what does an empty set of choices mean?
What changes when the generator opens extra connectors after carving its spanning tree?
How does the BFS distance limit keep the selected ring within useful hook range?
Which part of the hook trajectory makes it clear walls, and which part makes it meet the ring?
Why is the ring's base floor position saved before the next maze is generated?
Which state belongs to the shared session resource, and which state belongs to each hook or ring entity?
practice_tasks: Change START_CELLS and MAX_CELLS, then watch how maze scale changes with ring count.
Adjust the extra passage formula and compare dead ends with alternate routes.
Change the hook arc height. Find the smallest height that clears every wall.
Adjust HOOK_CATCH_RADIUS and HOOK_SPEED, then explain how the segment check prevents tunneling.
Change the maximum BFS distance and compare ring placement distance with hook usability.
Add a brief teleport flash at the saved ring position before drawing the next maze.
